questions.key_step: On $(0,1)$ the integer part $[-x]$ is the constant $-1$, so only the two joints $x=0$ and $x=1$ need checking.
questions.justification: Direct joint checks; greatest-integer constant on (0,1) is the only point.

questions.key_step: Split the logarithm and use $\frac{\ln(1+t)}{t}\to1$ so that each part contributes $2xe^{-2x}$ or $2xe^{-x}$.
questions.justification: Log/trig standard limits chained with a (1-cos2x)^2 denominator; several routine steps, no insight.

questions.key_step: Left of $2$ the quotient is the constant $-\lambda/\mu$, and right of $2$ we have $[x]=2$, so the exponent is $\frac{\tan h}{h}\to1$.
questions.justification: One-sided limits with an absolute value and a greatest-integer exponent; routine chain.

questions.key_step: Both sides are exponentials: the left one is a $1^\infty$ form giving $e^{3a}$, the right one has exponent $\frac{\tan2x}{\tan4x}\to\frac12$.
questions.justification: 1^infinity limit on one side and a tan ratio on the other; each standard.

questions.key_step: The running maximum of $\sin t$ equals $\sin x$ up to $\frac\pi2$, then stays $1$; the joints $\frac\pi2$ and $\pi$ have matching values and slopes.
questions.justification: Running maximum must be unfolded; two joints, slope check.

questions.key_step: The running maximum of the cubic follows it up to its local maximum at $t=1$, then stays flat at $1$; only the joint with $4-x$ at $x=3$ has unequal slopes.
questions.justification: Cubic running maximum piecewise; find peak, compare slopes at two joints.

questions.key_step: $f$ is a continuous 'tent', so $g$ is continuous everywhere; the corners of the two shifted tents are $-4,-2,0$ and $0,2,4$, and the corner at $0$ cancels.
questions.justification: Shifted tents; piecewise g and graph, cancellation of the corner at 0.

questions.key_step: Since $\sin(x-2)\to0$, continuity forces $P(2)=0$, and then $\frac{P(x)}{x-2}\to7$ pins down the linear factor.
questions.justification: Forcing P(2)=0 then solve two linear equations; one familiar move.

questions.key_step: $x-[x]=\{x\}$ and $1+[x]-x=1-\{x\}$, so $f$ is a continuous zig-zag with corners at the integers and at the half-integers.
questions.justification: Zig-zag min of fractional parts; count corners, no discontinuities.

questions.key_step: $h(x)=\min(\{x\},1-\{x\})$ is a continuous zig-zag with a corner at every integer and every half-integer.
questions.justification: Same zig-zag; check four options and count 7 corners.

questions.key_step: $9x^2-12x+4=(3x-2)^2\ge0$, so the exponential factor is smooth and positive; only the zeros of $x^2-2x-3$ can be corners.
questions.justification: Modulus times smooth positive factor; simple zeros only.

questions.key_step: Rationalise the right-hand piece to get $-4$; the left-hand piece splits into two standard limits $\frac1a+\frac1b$.
questions.justification: Rationalise one side, standard log limit on the other.

questions.key_step: $\tan2x-\sin2x=\tan2x(1-\cos2x)\sim2x\cdot2x^2=4x^3$, so the right-hand limit is $\frac4b$.
questions.justification: tan-sin limit; one standard limit plus a sine value.

questions.key_step: Only the integers $-1,0,1$ can be points of discontinuity (where $[x]$ jumps); on each interval $[n,n+1)$ the function is a fixed smooth expression.
questions.justification: Greatest-integer piecewise with a trig term; unfold four pieces and test three integers, errors easy.

questions.key_step: Reduce $f$ to explicit pieces: on $(-1,1)$ it is $\max(2x,0)$; then only $x=-1,0,1$ need checking.
questions.justification: Three-part function with GIF and max; check -1, 0, 1 and count both continuity and differentiability.

questions.key_step: $g\circ f$ is differentiable at $0$ only if it is continuous there; match values and one-sided slopes at $x=0$ to get $k_1,k_2$.
questions.justification: Composite of piecewise functions; correct active pieces, continuity then slope matching, then evaluation.

questions.key_step: $x\sin x\ge0$ on $[0,\pi]$ and $\le0$ on $[\pi,2\pi]$, so $f=1$ on $[0,\pi]$ and $f=1+x\sin x$ on $[\pi,2\pi]$.
questions.justification: min with 1; sign of x sin x then one derivative check.

questions.key_step: The constants $a$ and $b+c$ are fixed by the joints $x=0$ and $x=2$; the joint $x=1$ is discontinuous for every $a,b$.
questions.justification: Four-piece GIF function with parameters; statement analysis, key fact that x=1 is always discontinuous.

questions.key_step: Find which piece of $f$ is active: $g<0$ only for $0<x<2$, where $f(g)=[g]=-1$, while $f(0)=1$ and $f(2)=1$ force jumps at $0$ and $2$.
questions.justification: Composite with GIF; identify active pieces of f and test the points where g crosses 0.

questions.key_step: On $(-1,1)$ the floor of $4x^2-1$ jumps each time $4x^2-1$ crosses the integers $0,1,2$; add the joints $x=\pm1$.
questions.justification: GIF of a quadratic; counting crossing points plus joints with no options to check.

questions.key_step: $(f\circ g)(x)=[2g(x)^2]+1$ jumps once for every integer value that $2g^2$ passes through, on each side of $0$.
questions.justification: Composite of GIF of a squared two-branch function; count 31+31 integer crossings with the x=0 subtlety, no options.

questions.key_step: The two logarithms combine to $\ln(1+x^2+x^4)$ and $\sec x-\cos x=\frac{\sin^2x}{\cos x}$, so the quotient behaves like $\frac{x^2}{x^2}$.
questions.justification: Combine logs and use sin^2/cos form; one standard limit.

questions.key_step: Continuity at $x=0$ fixes $a=4$ and $b=-15$; then evaluate each composite by pieces.
questions.justification: Fix a,b by continuity then evaluate two compositions; routine.

questions.key_step: The denominator $\to0$, so the numerator must vanish: $p\cdot3^6=3^7$ gives $p=3$; then factor out $(1+\frac{x}{729})^{1/7}-1$ and $(1+\frac{qx}{729})^{1/3}-1$.
questions.justification: Force p=3 then binomial limit; a few chained standard steps.

questions.key_step: Treat $|x|<1$, $|x|>1$ and $x=\pm1$ separately (the limit of $x^{2n}$ is $0,\infty,1$); then compare left limit, value and right limit at $\pm1$.
questions.justification: Limit of a function containing x^{2n}; three regimes and three-value check at x=+-1.

questions.key_step: $|t|\sin|t|=t\sin t$ and $\cos|t|=\cos t$ are smooth; only $(x-3)|(x-1)(x-4)|$ has corners, at $x=1$ and $x=4$.
questions.justification: Modulus terms: even-function identities then simple-zero rule; each step routine but easy to misjudge x=2.

questions.key_step: Each logarithm gives a limit $\frac{\ln(1+kx)}{x}\to k$, so the limit is $5-\alpha$.
questions.justification: Single standard log limit.

questions.key_step: On $(\frac14,\frac12)$ the function is the floor of a strictly decreasing quadratic (a staircase), outside it equals the quadratic itself; check the two ends and the step.
questions.justification: GIF of a quadratic inside a two-branch function; jump at 1/4 and at the step plus a corner at 1/2; no options.

questions.key_step: $[x]$ jumps at integers and $[x+\frac12]$ jumps at half-integers: every such point is a non-differentiability point; the corner of $|2x+3|$ at $-\frac32$ lies on one of them.
questions.justification: Counting non-differentiable points from two floor functions and a modulus; double counting is the trap; numerical.
